title: The Gentleman Bandit Caught by His Laundry
topic: The Gentleman Bandit Caught by His Laundry
mechanism: City laundries stamped a private code on every customer's linen and kept a book of who owned each code, so one marked handkerchief (F.X.O.7) dropped at a robbery led the detectives straight to the bandit's name.

beats.hook: He robbed twenty-eight stagecoaches, and he was finally caught by his laundry: the camera glides down a dusty road onto a halted coach and a gentleman with a sack over his head.
beats.but: He never fired a shot, left poems, and nobody ever saw his face; the detectives had nothing.
beats.then: By day he was Charles Bolton, a gentleman in mining with fine white shirts.
beats.conflict: In 1883 a young man fires at him; he is barely grazed, flees, and drops a handkerchief in the bushes.
beats.pivot: You see, every city laundry stamped its own code on your linen and kept a book of codes and customers.
beats.so: So the detectives carry the handkerchief from laundry to laundry until a clerk reads the code: Mister Bolton.
beats.closing: Twenty-eight robberies without a single shot, undone by one dirty handkerchief.

seed.what: Bart's white handkerchief, tucked in his breast pocket from the first shot
